content: Data: We evaluate the spell correctors from § "Robust Word Recognition" on movie reviews from the Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST) BIBREF24 . The SST dataset consists of 8544 movie reviews, with a vocabulary of over 16K words. As a background corpus, we use the IMDB movie reviews BIBREF25 , which contain 54K movie reviews, and a vocabulary of over 78K words. The two datasets do not share any reviews in common. The spell-correction models are evaluated on their ability to correct misspellings. The test setting consists of reviews where each word (with length $\ge 4$ , barring stopwords) is attacked by one of the attack types (from swap, add, drop and keyboard attacks). In the all attack setting, we mix all attacks by randomly choosing one for each word. This most closely resembles a real world attack setting.
